title: Degraded-mode SLA definitions and adaptive escalation playbook for hybrid deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define formal SLA and SLO behavior for 'degraded mode' (partial capability) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, and produce an adaptive escalation/playbook tied to error-budget consumption and tenant-level contracts. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout gates, and observability/alerting needs required to ship a customer-facing SLA playbook and Console controls for progressive degradation and remediation.

Background and motivation: Customers who run latency-sensitive features require predictable behavior when we cannot meet primary SLOs (e.g., due to region capacity, kernel regressions, or KV cache disruptions). Instead of a binary pass/fail, we want to specify allowed degraded states (reduced throughput, longer percentile latency, fallbacks to cheaper model variants, or partial feature disablement) and connect those states to contractual SLA language and automated escalation. This is especially important for Private/VPC deployments where operator remediation may be manual.

Scope:
- Define 3-tier operational SLO bands per workload class (Realtime Chat, Generation, Embeddings): Green (optimal), Amber (degraded but functional), and Red (unavailable/auto-failover).
- Map customer contractual SLAs to allowed degraded bands and financial/operational remedies.
- Define error-budget burn rules and adaptive escalation actions at tier thresholds (25%, 50%, 75% consumed in sliding 1h window).
- Specify console UI/alerting hooks: tenant-level SLO dashboard, immediate PagerDuty thresholds, and customer-visible incident messages.
- Acceptance criteria and testplan for canary rollouts and policy enforcement in Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Out-of-scope: pricing/legal SLA verbage negotiations; on-prem installation packaging (this ticket creates the operational spec only).

Operational definitions and numeric targets (proposed):
- Workload classes and baseline SLOs (Green):
  - Realtime Chat (P50/P90/P99): 40ms / 120ms / 300ms; availability 99.95% (rolling 30d).
  - Generation (P50/P90/P99): 60ms / 220ms / 500ms; availability 99.9% (rolling 30d).
  - Embeddings (P50/P90/P99): 30ms / 100ms / 300ms; availability 99.9% (rolling 30d).
- Amber (degraded) band allowed under severe stress or capacity constraints:
  - Realtime Chat Amber: P90 <= 350ms, P99 <= 800ms, availability >= 99.5% (rolling 30d).
  - Generation Amber: P90 <= 500ms, P99 <= 1200ms, availability >= 99.0%.
  - Embeddings Amber: P90 <= 300ms, P99 <= 700ms, availability >= 99.0%.
- Red band: Service-level fallback triggered; customers should be routed to backup region/model or receive 503-like graceful degradation. Availability < Amber thresholds triggers Red.

Error budget and adaptive escalation rules (high-level):
- Compute error budget as 1 - availability SLO over a 30d rolling window.
- Deploy adaptive escalation when short-window burn is observed:
  - Alert tier1 (on-call) at 25% of 30d error budget consumed in last 1h.
  - Trigger automated traffic reduction / non-critical feature disables + PM notification at 50% burn in 1h.
  - Initiate customer-visible degraded mode + engage SE/Account team and open incident bridge at 75% burn in 1h.
  - Automatic rollback to last known-good model variant or cross-region failover if error budget exceeds 90% in any sliding 2h window.

Rollout gates and canary strategy (requirements):
- Gate A: Unit and integration tests for degraded-mode behaviors (simulated latency, failed KV access, model fallback).
- Gate B (canary): 5% traffic in Hosted region + one Dedicated pool for 48h with monitoring for SLO regressions; must not exceed historical baseline P99 increase by >25% or burn >10% of monthly error budget.
- Gate C (tenant opt-in): For Private deployments, provide an 'enable-degraded-mode' operator flag and a dry-run mode that logs decisions without taking action; operations must manually confirm before active enforcement.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before moving to In Review):
acceptance_criteria: Spec document published to Confluence with concrete SLO numbers, band definitions, and mapping to SLA contract language (link included below).
Console changes: tenant-level SLO dashboard shows current band (Green/Amber/Red) and live error-budget burn with historical trend; staging UI mocks approved by design.
Automated escalation logic implemented in runtime control plane with unit tests and integration tests that simulate burn scenarios.
Canary run plan and rollback plan documented; canary run executed in at least one hosted region and one dedicated pool without violating canary thresholds.
Private deployment operator flag implemented and tested in dry-run mode with on-prem testing checklist completed.
Runbook & PagerDuty playbook authored: steps for triage, mitigation (traffic-shift, model fallback, capacity scale), customer communications template, and postmortem checklist.
test_plan: Synthetic load tests to exercise Amber and Red bands and validate automated responses (traffic reduction, fallback).
Fault injection for KV cache and model serving errors to validate detection and escalation timers.
Tenant-level end-to-end verification: verify that opt-in tenants in Private mode receive only dry-run logs until operator flips the enforcement flag.
Audit and observability check: ensure all decision points are logged to tenant audit trail and that traces link to Console incident view.
